chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the monkey from being bought or sold.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying and selling monkeys in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific prohibition on the commercial trade of monkeys (al-qird), reflecting the broader Islamic economic principle of ensuring that sold items possess intrinsic utility and value. Within Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often contextualized within discussions of 'gharar' (uncertainty) or the distinct nature of animals as commodities, distinguishing them from livestock or poultry typically permitted in trade. It underscores the Prophet’s authority in regulating market practices to maintain ethical standards in commercial exchanges.
